newsitem.title: CHINA: Local investors snap up China's latest bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Local investors snap up China's latest bond issue.

text.p: Local investors snapped up China's last batch of treasury bonds for 1996 after they went on sale on Friday, with most sales outlets selling out in less than half a day, the Shanghai Securities News said on Saturday.
Underwriters, including securities houses and banks, sold the seven-year T-bonds at a coupon of 8.56 percent, 1.09 percentage points above the annual rate for one-year bank deposits.

With demand far exceeding supply, investors queued outside underwriting offices before dawn on Friday, the newspaper said. Most securities houses and banks in Shanghai were forced to limit the amount that each investor could buy.
"Most sales outlets had sold out all they had before noon yesterday," the newspaper said. It gave no further details.
Analysts consider the coupon on this batch of bonds attractive for investors because of a possible drop in bank interest rates again next year due to falling inflation.
Interest on the new bonds will be calculated as from November 1 and will be paid on an annual basis instead of at maturity, allowing buyers to re-invest, they said.
A total of 20 billion yuan ($2.41 billion) worth of the bonds are being issued from Friday to November 20.
